title: Six strings, two directions
summary: Number from thin to thick; name from thick to thin.

steps.title: Six strings, two directions
steps.body:
**string** means one of the six thin wires stretched along a guitar

**Why it matters:** Knowing which wire to use makes instructions easy to follow.

The thickest string is number 6; the thinnest is number 1. In this course their names, thick to thin, are E, A, D, G, B, E. Remember: **Eddie Ate Dynamite, Good Bye Eddie**. These letters name sounds; you do not need to read music. The two E strings sound different: one low, one high.

steps.title: Look and listen
steps.body: The picture puts string 1 at the top and string 6 at the bottom. On your guitar, find the thickest string first. Say 6 E, 5 A, 4 D, 3 G, 2 B, 1 E. Hear the low and high E sounds.

items.prompt: Which letter names the lit thickest string?

steps.title: Take your time
steps.body: Point at string 6, then string 1. Say the mnemonic slowly. Do not worry about playing anything yet.
